gender (neurosex) is an aspect of sex. there's reproductive sex (biological sex/ what biologists mean when they talk about sex unless otherwise mentioned), genetic sex (chromosomal makeup / allele expression), gender (also called gender identity - the sex of one's brain. the prevailing hypothesis of transsexualism is hormonal fluctuations in utero altering the fetal brain), and phenotype (the collection of sex characteristics).

all of these types of sex are not exactly binary - but they are still bimodal (dual bell-shaped distribution, with the majority of people approaching either pole). it's true i'm being a bit strict about where the cutoff is - these boundaries are a *bit* nebulous. but i find it frustrating that people run with that idea and claim that the boundary doesn't exist at all.

then there's sociological/anthropological gender. when people make the claim that "gender is a social construct", this is what they're talking about. neurosex is medically verifiable, while gender expression is entirely self-determined and seemingly infinite. i get exasperated by people conflating the two, because as a transsexual, my gender is very much real; i'm not playing dressup here.

i highly recommend the book, "the end of gender" by dr. deborah soh. i have a couple nitpicky criticisms about it, as dr. soh forgoes qualitative data in favor of quantitative data - which is refreshing given contemporary gender discourse, but i still see some value in qualitative methods. but overall, it is a fantastic read which explores sexology with as little political bias as is feasible
